```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# ==============================================================================
# LECTURER SETUP & PACKAGES
# ==============================================================================
library(readr)          # For importing CSV datasets
library(dplyr)          # For data manipulation and filtering
library(ggplot2)        # For graphic grammar and plotting
library(sf)             # For Simple Features spatial data handling
library(rnaturalearth)  # For fetching vector map boundaries
library(viridis)        # For accessible, colorblind-friendly color palettes

# Central comparative country vector
countries_to_compare <- c(
  "Jamaica",
  "Canada",
  "United States",
  "India",
  "Brazil",
  "Spain",
  "Nigeria",
  "South Africa"
)
```

# Introduction: Spatial Analysis in Social Science

Welcome to Lab 2!

In Lab 1, we examined development indicators across time using panel line graphs. However, national development is not evenly distributed across space. Geographic proximity, regional trade blocs, historical colonial boundaries and ecological zones heavily shape human development outcomes.

In this lab, we transition from time-series charts to **choropleth maps** (maps where geographical areas are coloured according to an underlying metric).

::: callout-note
### Learning Objectives

Upon completing this workbook, you will learn how to: 1. Load spatial vector data (country boundaries) using `sf` and `rnaturalearth`. 2. Execute spatial joins (`left_join`) combining map geometries with tabular OWID datasets. 3. Render choropleth maps using `ggplot2` and `geom_sf()`. 4. Apply cartographic projections suitable for global analysis.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Module 1: Fetching Spatial Geometries & Projections

## Spatial Data in R: Simple Features (`sf`)

In GIS (Geographic Information Systems), spatial data consists of: \* **Attributes:** The tabular numerical metrics (e.g., life expectancy in years). \* **Geometries:** Coordinates defining lines and polygons that draw borders on a map.

In R, the `sf` package stores geometries inside a dedicated column named `geometry`.

```{r}
#| label: load-world-map
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Fetch medium-resolution world country map geometries
world_map <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

# Inspect spatial dataframe structure
glimpse(world_map |> select(name, iso_a3, continent, geometry))
```

::: callout-important
### Cartographic Projections & Northern Bias

Because the Earth is a 3D sphere, flattening it onto a 2D screen requires a mathematical projection.

The traditional **Mercator projection** distorts land area at high latitudes, visually expanding North America and Europe while shrinking Africa, South America, and South Asia. From a Global South perspective, projection choice is inherently political. It shapes how spatial scales are perceived.
:::

# Module 2: Mapping Global Health Inequalities

## Merging Geometries with Tabular Data

We can join our spatial `world_map` object with `life_expectancy_data.csv` using the 3-letter ISO country code (`iso_a3` in `sf` and `Code` in OWID).

```{r}
#| label: join-health-data
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Import health metrics from root data folder
life_exp_data <- read_csv("data/life_expectancy_data.csv")

# Isolate 2021 health metrics
life_exp_2021 <- life_exp_data |>
  filter(Year == 2021) |>
  rename(life_expectancy = 4)

# Execute spatial left join
world_health_map <- world_map |>
  filter(continent != "Antarctica") |>
  left_join(life_exp_2021, by = c("iso_a3" = "Code"))
```

## Global Health Choropleth Map

```{r}
#| label: fig-global-life-exp-map
#| fig-cap: "Figure 1: Global distribution of period life expectancy at birth in years (2021)."
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-align: center

ggplot(world_health_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = life_expectancy), color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "magma",
    na.value = "grey90",
    name = "Life Expectancy (Years)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Global Life Expectancy Inequities (2021)",
    subtitle = "Period life expectancy at birth across national economies",
    caption = "Source: Our World in Data / UN World Population Prospects."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Module 3: Comparative Spatial Zoom — Regional Focus

We can filter our spatial dataset to examine intra-regional variance across **Latin America & Caribbean** and **Sub-Saharan Africa**.

```{r}
#| label: fig-regional-health-map
#| fig-cap: "Figure 2: Regional breakdown of life expectancy across Africa and South America."
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-align: center

regional_map <- world_health_map |>
  filter(continent %in% c("Africa", "South America"))

ggplot(regional_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = life_expectancy), color = "white", size = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", na.value = "grey85", name = "Years") +
  facet_wrap(~continent) +
  labs(
    title = "Intra-Regional Health Divergence (2021)",
    subtitle = "Comparative spatial breakdown across Africa and South America",
    caption = "Source: Our World in Data."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "cm"),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

# Student Coding Lab Exercises

Complete these four exercises in your R environment to practice your spatial pipeline skills.

### Exercise 1: Filter Specific Case Study Countries

``` r
# EXERCISE 1: Filter and map our 8 core comparative cases
target_map <- world_health_map |>
  filter(name %in% c("Jamaica", "Canada", "United States", "India", 
                     "Brazil", "Spain", "Nigeria", "South Africa"))

ggplot(target_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = life_expectancy)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma") +
  labs(title = "Life Expectancy across Comparative Case Studies") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Exercise 2: Map Education Stock Metrics

``` r
# EXERCISE 2: Import, join, and map education data for 2020
edu_data <- read_csv("data/education_data.csv") |>
  filter(Year == 2020) |>
  rename(schooling = 4)

world_edu_map <- world_map |>
  filter(continent != "Antarctica") |>
  left_join(edu_data, by = c("iso_a3" = "Code"))

ggplot(world_edu_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = schooling), color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "cividis", name = "Years") +
  labs(
    title = "Global Mean Years of Schooling (2020)",
    subtitle = "Adult educational attainment stock across national economies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Exercise 3: Audit Missing Spatial Data

``` r
# EXERCISE 3: Audit spatial missingness by continent
missing_by_continent <- world_health_map |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarise(
    total_countries = n(),
    missing_health  = sum(is.na(life_expectancy))
  )

missing_by_continent
```

### Exercise 4: Reproject Map Coordinate Reference Systems

``` r
# EXERCISE 4: Reproject map geometries to Robinson projection
world_robinson <- st_transform(world_health_map, crs = "+proj=robin")

ggplot(world_robinson) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = life_expectancy), color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma") +
  labs(title = "Global Life Expectancy (Robinson Projection)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
